L232: Post Degree programs
L233: 
L234: Douglas College is the leading provider of post-degree programs in British Columbia. As an international student at Douglas College, you have the opportunity to pursue a one-year Post Degree Diploma (PDD) or two-year Post Baccalaureate Diploma (PBD).
L235: Since you already have a degree, we know that you're looking for a program that will provide you with advanced skills that build upon your existing education. Our rigorous post-degree programs are comprised of upper-level courses that will equip you with the skills and knowledge that employers are looking for. You'll earn a recognized credential that can help you get a job, take your career in a new direction, expand your earning potential and, for working professionals, upgrade and broaden your skills.
L236: Admission to these programs requires that you have a bachelor's degree.

L52: ## On this page
L53: 
L54:   * cite14†How to meet the field of study requirement L55:   * cite15†Check if your CIP code is eligible L56:   * cite16†Check the list of currently eligible CIP codes L57:   * cite17†Search for your CIP code L58: ## How to meet the field of study requirement
L59: 
L60: You must graduate from a program that’s on the list of currently eligible cite18†Classification of Instructional Programs (CIP) codes when you submit your
L61: 
L62:   * study permit application or
L63:   * PGWP application
L64: Eligible fields of study are linked to certain jobs in long-term shortage in Canada and can change based on the needs of the Canadian labour market. If your CIP code is not on the list of currently eligible codes when you apply for a PGWP, it may still be eligible based on when you submitted your study permit application.
L65: 
L66: What’s a CIP code?
L67: 
L68: A CIP code is a number we use to classify post-secondary education programs according to the field of study.
L69: For PGWP eligibility, we use 6-digit CIP codes based on the cite19†CIP Canada 2021†www.statcan.gc.ca (opens in a new tab).
L70: 
L71: To find your program’s CIP code, you can
L72:   * check your designated learning institution’s (DLI) website
L73:     * Most DLIs have information about PGWP eligibility and CIP codes on their website.
L74:   * contact your DLI
L75:     * Contact your DLI for more information about the program and applicable 6-digit CIP codes if you have any questions.
L76:   * search the cite20†Statistics Canada CIP classification catalogue†www23.statcan.gc.ca and find the 6-digit code that’s most applicable
L77:     * Search by keyword or by navigating through the available links in the main table.
L78:     * Program titles can be broad. Read the description, illustrative examples and exceptions found on the individual results to make sure your program matches.
L79: ## Check if your CIP code is eligible
L80: 
L81: To meet the field of study requirement, your CIP code must be on the list of currently eligible CIP codes when you submit either your study permit application or your PGWP application.
L82: ### PGWP field of study list freeze for 2026
L83: 
L84: For 2026, we won’t add or remove any eligible fields of study.
